items.description: The Gargaf Mountains are a rugged and arid mountain range in central Libya, known for their harsh environment.
The Mizdah Plateau is a vast limestone plateau in western Libya, named after the town of Mizdah.
The foothills of the Tibesti Mountains offer a dramatic landscape on Libya's southern border with Chad.
Sarir Tanezrouft is an extremely dry and flat desert plain, often described as a 'land of terror' due to its desolation.
Al-Haruj is a massive field of black volcanic rock in central Libya, one of the largest such fields in the Sahara.
Jebel Aswad, meaning 'Black Mountain', is a volcanic massif in the Fezzan region of southwestern Libya.
The Gargaf Desert is a stony desert region characterized by its high plateaus and dry riverbeds.
Wadi Mathendous is world-renowned for its prehistoric rock art, featuring large-scale engravings of wild animals.
The Cyrenaica Coast features some of Libya's most lush and green Mediterranean landscapes.
Wadi Farigh is a desert valley in the northeast, known for its unique geology and seasonal importance.
Jebel Tarhuna is a hilly region southeast of Tripoli, famous for its olive groves and agricultural productivity.
The mountains around Ghat are part of the Akakus range, famous for their spectacular scenery and rock art.
